name: Code
purpose: Present a short inline technical literal with native code semantics and a finished Brick technical-text recipe.
useWhen: A short identifier, attribute, command, filename, value, or API name belongs inside prose or a compact label.

avoidWhen.condition: The source is multi-line, preserves whitespace, needs language metadata, or may scroll.
The content represents keyboard input, computer output, a variable, editable source, or executable source.
avoidWhen.useInstead: the correct native semantic element or an application-owned editor, terminal, or sandbox

composition: Keep Code inside the surrounding Text or component content owner when the literal completes that sentence or label.
Choose subtle for an independently visible inline token and plain with tone inherit when the surrounding component already owns paint and foreground.

rules.statement: Use Code only for a short computer-code fragment and preserve its one native code host; do not select it merely to obtain monospace typography.
Keep Code inline with the prose or compact label it completes and use Code Block for multi-line or overflow-owned technical source.
Choose variant, tone, and size through the closed Code recipes before overriding public variables; use tone inherit when a parent intentionally owns foreground contrast.
Load styles.css or core.css plus code.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using generic Text or a native span with monospace CSS for a real technical literal.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Code so the literal keeps native code semantics and the shared Brick technical recipe.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting a complete diff, command transcript, or configuration example inside Code.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Code Block so preserved whitespace, naming, focus, and overflow have one explicit owner.

validation: Confirm one native code element, correct surrounding sentence flow, safe wrapping of long tokens, and no unintended block or scroll behavior.
Check inherited typography, subtle and plain recipes, light and dark appearances, forced colors, zoom, localization, RTL/bidi content, and CSS delivery.
